Subject: LLM performance & deployment recap — Optima Health discovery

Miguel — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please confirm or correct anything I've mis-stated.

Key pain points you shared:
- Latency spikes during morning peak (08:00–10:30 local) causing degraded UI responsiveness.
- Need production SLOs for the patient-facing summarization feature: low-latency short prompts and higher-throughput batch/async tasks.
- Strong data residency / HIPAA requirements; VPC-only access preferred.
- Cost sensitivity for large-scale async workloads; opportunity to route lower-critical traffic to cheaper model variants.

Stated targets from the call:
- Short prompts (<=80 tokens): target p50 ~200–300 ms, p95 <= 800 ms (example target you mentioned was ~250ms p50).
- Long inference / summarization (>=512 tokens): acceptable p95 up to ~2s with predictable tail behavior.
- Peak concurrency: 300–400 qps for web-facing summaries; average sustained 90–150 qps.
- Tokenization mix: ~30% short (chat-like), 70% multi-paragraph summarization.

Initial topology/fit notes (high level):
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool in your cloud region) to meet predictable p50/p95 SLOs + VPC peering for HIPAA controls.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts in the triage flow to reduce downstream token cost.
- Multi-variant routing: primary low-latency model for web, fallback/multi-quantized variants for batch processing.

Immediate next steps we proposed on the call:
1) You to confirm the SLO numbers above are the right targets (p50/p95 + peak qps).
2) Optima to share a small prompt set and a tokenization sample (10–20 representative prompts).
3) Redwood to run a 1-hour synthetic perf test (controlled load) and share results + a short mutual action plan (MPA).
4) Schedule a dedicated technical deep-dive (infra + security + ML ops) to align on networking and rollout cadence.

Attachments: optima_mpa_notes.pdf (notes from today's call / draft MPA)

If that all looks right, I'm proposing we schedule the tech deep-dive next week (Wed/Thu preferred) — I'm dropping a Calendly link below in the follow-up.

Thanks,

Jordan — thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications and additions from our side:

Clarifications / corrections:
- The 200–300ms p50 window is our ideal for short prompts (patient-facing blips) — realistic target is ~250ms p50. We can't guarantee p95 < 800ms for all short prompts today; 800ms is a hard upper bound for user-facing interactions.
- For long summaries, p95 ~2s is acceptable, but we want tight variance; occasional 3–4s is okay for very long docs.
- Peak concurrency: the 300–400 qps is accurate during product marketing campaigns; baseline weekday peak is closer to 280 qps.

Security/residency:
- Confirmed: VPC peering required, data must remain in our dedicated VPC and be logged for audit (we'll need access to request logs / token-level traces for SOC / incident workups).

Files I'm sharing:
- optima_latency_sample.log (small sample of latency spikes from last campaign) — FYI only, shows clustering around 09:15 local.

Scheduling:

1) Can Redwood provide an expected cost delta between hosted vs dedicated for our expected volume? A rough $/1M tokens estimate is enough.
2) Do you support on-prem / air-gapped options if we need later?

Happy to proceed — please include a short pre-read for the deep-dive (topology sketch + required network ports and IAM assumptions).

Miguel — perfect, thanks for the details and the sample log. Short technical pre-read below so your infra/security leads can scan before the deep-dive.

High-level topology recommendation (pre-read):
- Deployment mode: Redwood Dedicated in your cloud account (GCP us-west1) with VPC peering. This gives predictable GPUs, dedicated KV cache, and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM.
- Routing: single endpoint with policy-based routing — latency-critical calls hit the low-latency model (FP16 / optimized kernels), non-critical async summarization hits a quantized 4-bit variant. Automated fallback to a compatible variant if latency SLOs are threatened.
- Caching + batching: enable prefix + KV cache for the triage flow (we saw ~35–45% token reduction in similar customers). Continuous batching window tuned to 10–25ms to balance throughput vs p50 latency.
- Model & quantization: recommend starting with an open LLM v1.2 (FP16) for primary path, evaluate a 4-bit quantized variant for async jobs. Kernel selection will be tuned by sequence-length distribution from your prompt sample.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and trace links exported to your tracing backend (or Redwood Console). Logs and request metadata can be sent to your GCS/Splunk bucket via VPC egress config.

Answers to your questions:
1) Cost delta: rough estimate for your steady-state (120–150 qps avg, peak 300 qps): Hosted: ~$1.8k–2.4k / 1M tokens (managed, includes selection of multi-tenant savings). Dedicated (reserved): ~$0.9k–1.3k / 1M tokens depending on commitment and chosen quantization. We'll formalize after we see the prompt/token mix.
2) On-prem / air-gapped: yes — Redwood Private supports on-prem packages and HSM/KMS integrations. That is a longer onboarding path (legal + infra) but available.

Proposed immediate playbook:
- Optima: share 10–20 representative prompts + tokenization counts (you already noted you'll do this).
- Redwood: run a 1-hour perf test using your sample set (we'll exercise both low-latency and async routes), provide a results deck and an MPA draft. Target deliverable within 72 hours of receiving samples.
- Schedule technical deep-dive: I created tentative slots Wed 09:00–10:30 PT and Wed 10:30–12:00 PT — please confirm which one works for your infra lead.

Attachment: redwood-deploy-sketch.png (simple sketch of recommended VPC peering + routing)

If that lines up, I'll open a HubSpot MPA and leave action items there so we can track owners.

Thanks — Jordan
